today (cite `file:line` or a doc). Neutral; no recommendation yet.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | | | | |

The option chosen, in one or two sentences, and why it beat the others.

## 0. Document control  [F I S]

| | |
|---|---|
| Scope | Feature / Integration / Full system |
| Reviewers | the architects named in §12 |

## 1. Purpose  [F I S]

Why this change, in business terms, in one short paragraph plus three bullets. A reader who
knows nothing should finish this section able to say what gets better and for whom.

- **The demand:** what changes for which users (the profile's `users`). For an integration:
  the capability we need from the provider and why we are not building it. For the full
  system: what the system is for.
- **The capability it serves:** the `capability_map` part, or an entry in
  `business.capabilities`.
- **In scope / out of scope:** two short lists. Out of scope is the more useful one.

## 2. Audience  [F I S]

| Reader | The decision or action this document has to support |

---
title: <Name> Guide
status: Draft
owner: solution-architect
date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
---

# <emoji> <Name> Guide

> **What this is.** One paragraph: what this guideline governs, and the failure it exists
> to prevent. Write the failure concretely. A reader who has met that failure should
> recognize it here.

**Owner:** <team or architect> · **Applies to:** `<the folders it governs>` (`<the stack it assumes, from the profile's stack>`) · **Basis:** `<the primary sources, named with versions>`
* * *
## <Subject> at a glance

| Question | Answer | Where |
| ---| ---| --- |
| <the question a reader arrives with> | <the answer in one line> | §n |

Four to seven rows. This table exists so a narrow question can be answered without
reading the file, so every row is a question someone actually asks.

> 🎯 **The rule this guide is built on:** _one sentence._ If you cannot write it, the
> guideline does not have a spine yet and the sections will not hang together.

> ⚠️ **Scope.** What this guideline does **not** cover, and which guideline does. Name the
> file. A rule stated in two guidelines goes stale in one of them.

> 🚧 **Status.** Only if the guideline rests on a decision the decision maker has not taken. Say
> which decision, which rules change with it, and that the rest hold either way. Delete
> this box when the decision lands and the status moves to Agreed.
* * *
## 1. <The first section>

Numbered sections, `### 1.1` subsections. Number the rules too, and keep the numbers
stable, so a review comment can cite "rule 14" and a reader can find it.

### 1.1 <A subsection>

# Project profile for the virtual architecture team. BLANK COPY: fill it in.
#
# Copy to docs/architecture/project.yaml in your project. The architects in
# .claude/agents/ are generic; everything they know about your project comes from here.
# Fill what you know, leave "" where you don't yet, and the architects will ask for it.
# Delete a whole section only if it can never apply (say, `hosting` for a library).
# No secret values, ever: name the variable or the secret.

profile_version: 1

project:
  name: ""                 # product or company name, as users see it
  local_name: ""           # the name in the primary language, if different
  summary: ""              # two sentences: what it does, for whom
  stage: ""                # idea / pilot / live / scaling, and roughly how big
  team: ""                 # who builds and runs it
  decision_maker: ""       # who decides; architects recommend (e.g. "the CTO", "the head of engineering", "the architecture board")
  reply_language: ""       # e.g. "English", or "English, or the language of the message"
  naming_rules: []         # names to use or never use (legacy repo names, brand spelling)

users:                     # each kind of user, and what matters about them
  - name: ""
    notes: ""              # include anyone who cannot consent for themselves, such as children

languages:
  primary: ""              # include the script direction if RTL
  others: []
  notes: ""                # where translations live, RTL traps

business:
  capabilities: []         # what the business must be able to do, one line each
  contexts:                # bounded contexts, if you know them
    - name: ""
      owns: ""
      lives_in: ""         # modules or services in the code
  bias: ""                 # e.g. "smallest architecture a team of two can run"

stack:
  frontend: ""             # framework, version, folder
  backend: ""              # language, framework, structure, how dependencies are wired
